data.narrative:
QuEra Computing is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $230M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 comparable firms—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private, including Quantinuum, PsiQuantum, and SandboxAQ—though the private peer set at QuEra's stage and valuation tier lacks sufficient density for reliable multiples analysis.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($230M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $437M. This method is grounded in the empirical observation that quantum computing companies at this stage have historically commanded this magnitude of uplift as they progress past Series B milestones.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $371M to $503M, centered on $437M. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables with sufficient transparency to cross-validate via peer median multiples, and the nascent regulatory and technical landscape surrounding quantum hardware commercialization, which creates measurement challenges beyond traditional enterprise software or semiconductors. The single-method derivation narrows confidence relative to a fully triangulated approach, warranting sensitivity analysis around the 1.9x multiplier assumption.
